company_items.summary: AutoZone reported FQ4 EPS of $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-LIFO tailwind to gross margins. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year to 33.4% of sales. Linearity improved in the final 8 weeks of the quarter and management expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80-90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex more aggressively in the robotics and Physical AI space.

MillerKnoll posted solid FQ1 EPS of 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, implying organic EPS of 42 cents. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was trimmed to $3.88-4.03 billion from $3.93-4.13 billion, while EPS guidance was left unchanged at $1.85-2.15.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau previously served as CFO at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International, bringing significant large-cap industrial CFO experience to the role.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% vs. the Street's 13.85%, and management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure on household budgets. Revenue of $2.311 billion came in above the Street's $2.17 billion estimate but declined 8.4% year-over-year. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost reduction actions underway, and a roughly 75% surge in the North American towable RV order backlog.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after the company reported positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, including an impressive 22% weight loss outcome. The results represent a meaningful data readout for the company's obesity franchise and could reprice the stock significantly higher. This positions Viking as a more credible competitor in the increasingly crowded GLP-1 landscape.

sectors: RV/recreational vehicle sector faces macro headwinds per THOR management — stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation are pressuring household budgets and keeping retail soft. The GLP-1/obesity drug space gets a positive data point from Viking's VK2735 results. Industrial automation and robotics see M&A activity with Cognex acquiring RealSense.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is the company-specific earnings note for Tuesday, September 22nd. No broad macro or Fed commentary in today's note — this one is all about individual stock catalysts before the open, so let's get right into it.

Starting with Viking Therapeutics, the big pre-market mover. Shares are spiking after the company reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 weight loss drug, with patients achieving 22% weight loss. That's a strong data readout and puts Viking more firmly on the map as a legitimate competitor in the obesity drug space. Clearly bullish.

On AutoZone — the headline EPS beat looks solid at $56.05 versus the Street at $54.03, but dig into it and the quality is questionable. The upside was almost entirely driven by tariff refunds, a 145 basis point tailwind to gross margins, plus a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit. Meanwhile, domestic comps missed — plus 1.6% versus the Street's plus 3.1% — and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did note improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027, but this is a mixed read at best.

MillerKnoll delivered a cleaner beat — 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents — and importantly, they would have beaten even stripping out the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind. Orders were up 3.5% year-over-year. The negatives: sales missed at $923 million versus $943 million expected, and the fiscal 2027 revenue guidance range was trimmed slightly. EPS guidance held unchanged. Call it a net positive with some noise.

Cognex announced an acquisition of RealSense, the depth-sensing camera and vision technology leader for robotics and Physical AI, for around $500 million upfront plus roughly $106 million more. RealSense is expected to put up $80 to $90 million in revenue, growing more than 50% year-over-year. Bold move into the robotics perception space — bullish for the long-term thesis.

THOR Industries missed on the bottom line — 78 cents versus 87 cents expected. Gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%. Management was candid about the difficult backdrop: stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation are squeezing household budgets and keeping retail soft. They won't give formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall. Some silver linings — dealer inventory is healthy, structural cost actions are underway, and the North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year. But the overall picture is cautious.

And finally, Pentair named a new CFO — Bob Hau, effective November 1st. He comes with strong credentials, having previously been CFO at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. Routine leadership transition, largely a neutral event.

Bottom line for today: Viking is the standout name to watch on the long side. AutoZone's beat needs scrutiny given the quality issues. THOR is under pressure from a tough consumer spending backdrop in discretionary big-ticket categories. Stay disciplined and good luck out there.
